long_biography.plain_text:
ADCO began in 1972 as Bob Hill's construction enterprise and grew into a national builder working across commercial, public and industrial projects. Hill and Judy Brinsmead led the privately held group together, embedding a family ownership structure that now includes the next generation and a professional management team.

A separate opportunity arrived when Queensland authorities sought a developer for a marine precinct on the Brisbane River. Hill and Brinsmead reshaped the initial marina concept around refit, maintenance and specialist marine trades, opening Rivergate in 2006. The facility became a base for international refit work and a platform for Australia's wider marine-services sector. Hill remains a co-owner and director alongside Brinsmead and their son Tom.

A South Australian Game Fishing Association publication directly joins Bob Hill to Huntress, matching the source record's distinctive vessel relationship; ADCO, Rivergate and independent business sources then converge on the Australian construction and maritime founder. The former senator Robert Hill, basketball coach Bob Hill, police executive Bob Hill and unrelated Australian catalogue entrepreneur are excluded.

No strong public source supplied Hill's legal first name, middle names, exact birth date or birthplace. The public business record consistently uses Bob Hill, so no name expansion or birth field is proposed.

No dedicated Forbes profile was found. A Forbes article concerning a different Australian Robert Hill was rejected rather than used to resolve this owner, and no net-worth estimate or private-company valuation is included.

Construction & Engineering is directly established as the wealth-creation industry. Current Rivergate co-ownership is also established, but no source compares its value with any retained ADCO interest, and ADCO's current leadership page does not name Bob Hill. The primary industry therefore uses the mandatory construction origin-sector fallback without asserting proven present dominance.

Founder remains the current wealth relationship because Rivergate currently names Hill as co-owner and director of the facility he co-founded. The dossier does not assume that he retains a personal ADCO stake or day-to-day ADCO control merely because the wider company remains family-owned.

The family-succession test does not support inherited wealth. Sources identify Hill as ADCO's founder and Rivergate's co-founder, with no documented inheritance, gift, spousal transfer or succession into either core platform. His starting resources and family advantages are not described, so broad Self-made is used instead of an unsupported subtype.

Ship repair is the only approved active tag proposed. Rivergate's refit, maintenance and shipyard services meet its material operating-relationship test through Hill's current co-ownership and directorship. Superyacht construction is excluded because the sources describe service and refit operations rather than building superyachts; broader marine-engineering and family-business tags would be redundant or weaker.

No personal LinkedIn, Instagram, website, Facebook, Twitter/X, YouTube or TikTok profile met the two-point identity threshold. Rivergate's official site is proposed as a Company Website because it directly names Hill and his current formal relationship.

The biographies exclude Huntress and every vessel fact, changing company and project totals, transaction values, awards, rankings, private contact data, source narration and classification analysis. The long biography's mention of son Tom is limited to public business governance and not used to infer inheritance.

The short and long biographies were allocated independently. The short alone foregrounds Australian identity, the major-contractor result and continuing ownership; the long alone develops ADCO's project breadth, the government approach, Rivergate's concept shift, professional management and next-generation governance.
